svg.text: Wuxianmen V5 — Review and Revision-3 Detail Pass
2026-09-18 • BP_Wuxianmen_V5_4K_Core and BP_Wuxianmen_V5_FullPBR • materials and per-instance weathering only
7 components and 5,103 instance transforms per asset, all preserved • no map saved
Review — already fixed in revision 2
• Roof un-inverted on both tiers (180° about each mid-plane)
• Wood roof decks re-seated below the tiles
• Ridge re-bound to main_ridge and re-axed onto X
• Roof tile UV contract measured from the sheet
• Stone one-stone-per-block (Core) / magnified (FullPBR)
• Plaque textured (Core) / tint neutralised (FullPBR)
Confirmed by this review
ridge z 1572 cm, eave 1312 cm → rise +260 cm
FullPBR assembly identical to Core, byte for byte
Both assets re-validated before this pass touched them.
Pre-existing finding: FullPBR ships pattern-free sheets, so its roof
borrows the Core package's authored tile sheet (user decision).
Review — what was still missing
• Wood material never touched. One slot, UV0 of 0..1 per unit cube,
instances from 0.80 m to 22.59 m → the big pieces smear the sheet.
• Stone weathering shallow: per-instance tone only, no staining and
no moss, against a reference that is heavily weathered.
• Roof was one uniform surface — no weathered patches.
• Ridge cylinders reused the roof-strip UV contract, which maps
arbitrarily on a cylinder.
Wood instance sizes measured
n=451 min 0.80 m median 1.31 m max 22.59 m
269 instances exceed the 1.3 m reference size
So a single tiling cannot serve the role: the fix has to know each
instance's own size.
Review — suspicions that did not hold
Nanite fallback: already correct
The workflow asks for a full-triangle fallback with zero relative error
on thin roofs, tiles and caps. Measured on all seven meshes in both
variants:
enabled = True relative_error = 0.0 percent = 100.0
Verified and left alone — nothing to change.
Ridge ornaments: not buried after all
An earlier reading suggested the eight 0.35 m ornaments were buried by
the un-inversion. Measuring the corrected roof under each one with a
proper sampling window:
4 sit 3 cm above the lower roof (base 12.175 / roof 12.143)
4 sit 26 cm low inside the main roof (base 13.275 / roof 13.537)
Revision 3 — stone weathering
Per-instance custom data now carries three values, so the weathering is
deterministic and does not depend on where the asset is placed:
0 = UV offset 1 = wall height 0..1 2 = tone seed 0..1
Three layers added
• Wall-height stain: lerp(0.58 grey, white, saturate(height · 1.6)) — the
base of the wall darkens, as the reference shows.
• Wider per-instance tone: 0.72..1.22 (was 0.85..1.15).
• Moss: a restrained 0.38 blend toward 0.42/0.50/0.30, confined to the
lower band by saturate(1 − height · 2.2).
Measured inputs
wall height 0.0031..0.9476 across 4,213 instances — full range
Revision 3 — wood, tile tone and ridge cap
Wood gets a tiling from each instance's own size
tiling = 1 + custom_data · 16 where custom_data = (size/1.3 − 1)/16
A 1.3 m column is unchanged; a 22.5 m roof deck tiles 17x instead of
smearing the sheet across the whole span. Tint warmed from
0.43/0.27/0.17 to 0.78/0.56/0.40 — the timber read as flat dark maroon.
FullPBR's wood sheet is pattern-free, so it takes a fixed 0.3 tiling that
reads as soft grain rather than a per-instance one.
Roof tile tone variation
per-instance 0.86..1.16, breaking the uniform roof into weathered patches
Dedicated ridge cap material
U 5.127 along the axis (75 tiles, 0.30 m each) V 0.4646 around
Validation
• Every instance transform in both assets is byte-identical to the revision-3 baseline — this pass changes materials and custom data only, never placement.
• Component count 7, instance count 5,103, collision profile, visibility and shadow flags unchanged. Materials bound as expected on stone, wood, tile and ridge.
• Roof still rises to a ridge: 1572 cm at the centre vs 1312 cm at the eaves, rise +260 cm, in both variants.
Blocker — no new perspective review for this pass

The deferred high-res screenshot is still writing one stale frame for every requested view, in both variants. Already ruled out: camera readback, missing transient actors, editor_invalidate_viewports(), a 10 s delay, force_game_view off, an explicit CameraActor argument, and a SceneCapture2D render-target export. The editor window not being in the foreground remains the leading cause; Python cannot toggle that throttle.

Consequence: the revision-3 materials are measured and numerically validated but not visually confirmed. The capture set should be re-run with the editor foregrounded, and the plaque reading direction confirmed from a front-on view at the same time.
